meta.description: Knowledge base for the Nova rule-based chatbot. Every entry here is data: the engine in chatbot.py never hard-codes an intent.
notes: patterns: phrases the user might type. Matched in tiers: exact, then keyword (phrase inside a longer sentence), then fuzzy (typos).
exact_only: short or ambiguous phrases that should match only when the whole message equals them.
regex: named-group patterns for intents that need entity extraction. Groups become entities the handler can use.
reject: captured values that should not be accepted (used by the pattern tier to avoid false positives).
context: if present, the intent can only match when the previous matched intent is in this list.
handler: name of a dynamic handler in chatbot.py that computes placeholder values such as {time}.
responses: templates. Placeholders in braces are filled by the engine. Templates that need {user_name} are skipped until the user has shared a name.
alt_responses: used when a handler reports that the normal reply is not possible (for example, asking for a name that was never given).

goodbye_responses: Bye for now. Come back any time.
empty_input_response: Please type something so I can help you.

responses: I don't understand that yet. Could you rephrase it?
I'm not sure what you mean. Try asking something else, or type 'help' to see what I can do.
That is outside my rule set. Type 'help' to see the kinds of things I understand.

intents.name: greeting
intents.description: The user says hello.
responses: Hello! How can I help you today?
Hi there! What can I do for you?
Hey! Good to see you.
Hello, {user_name}! Nice to see you again.
Hi {user_name}! What can I do for you today?

intents.name: how_are_you
intents.description: The user asks how the bot is doing.
responses: I'm just a set of rules, but I'm running smoothly. How about you?
Doing well, thanks for asking. How are you?
All systems normal on my side. How is your day going?

intents.name: mood_good
intents.description: The user says they are doing well.
responses: That's good to hear!
Glad you're doing well.
Nice. What can I do for you?
Good to hear, {user_name}.

intents.name: mood_bad
intents.description: The user says they are not doing well.
responses: I'm sorry to hear that. I hope things get better soon.
That sounds tough. Take it easy on yourself.
Sorry you're feeling that way. If a joke would help, just ask for one.
I'm sorry, {user_name}. I hope the rest of your day is kinder.

intents.name: reciprocal
intents.description: The user turns a question back to the bot.
responses: I'm doing fine, thanks for asking.
Running smoothly, as always.
All good here.

intents.name: name
intents.description: The user asks who the bot is.
responses: I'm {bot_name}, a rule-based chatbot.
You can call me {bot_name}.
My name is {bot_name}. I answer using a fixed set of rules, no machine learning involved.

intents.name: time
intents.description: The user asks for the current time.
patterns: what is the time right now
responses: The current time is {time} (PKT).
It's {time} in Pakistan Standard Time.

intents.name: date
intents.description: The user asks for today's date.
responses: Today is {date}.
The date today is {date}.

intents.name: day
intents.description: The user asks which day of the week it is.
patterns: what day of the week is it
responses: Today is {day}.
It's {day} today.

intents.name: thanks
intents.description: The user thanks the bot.
responses: You're welcome!
Any time. Happy to help.
No problem at all.
You're welcome, {user_name}.

intents.name: help
intents.description: The user asks what the bot can do.
responses: I currently know {intent_count} intents. You can ask about my name, the time, the date, or the day, ask for a joke, a coin flip, a dice roll, or a bit of arithmetic like 12 * 7. Tell me your name and I'll remember it. Type 'list intents' to see everything.

intents.name: list_intents
intents.description: The user asks for the full list of intents.
responses: Here are the {intent_count} intents I know: {intent_list}.

intents.name: creator
intents.description: The user asks who built the bot.
responses: I was built by Shaikh Muhammad Zain as Project 1 of the DecodeLabs AI internship.
Shaikh Muhammad Zain wrote me in Python for the DecodeLabs AI internship.

intents.name: about_project
intents.description: The user asks what the bot is or how it works.
patterns: what language are you written in
what is a rule based chatbot
responses: I'm a rule-based chatbot written in Python. Every message goes through four steps: clean the text, look it up in a dictionary of known phrases, fall back to keyword and fuzzy matching, then pick a reply. There is no machine learning and no network call, so every answer is traceable to a rule.
No neural networks here. I map what you type to an intent using dictionary lookups, keyword search, and a fuzzy matcher for typos. If nothing matches, I say so instead of guessing.

intents.name: remember_name
intents.description: The user tells the bot their name.
regex: ^(?:my name is|my name's|call me|you can call me|i am called|this is|it's me|people call me|i go by) (?P<name>[a-z][a-z'\-]{1,30})$
responses: Nice to meet you, {user_name}! I'll remember that.
Hello {user_name}, good to meet you.
Got it, {user_name}. I'll keep that in mind for the rest of our chat.

intents.name: recall_name
intents.description: The user asks whether the bot remembers their name.
patterns: what did i say my name was
responses: Your name is {user_name}.
You told me your name is {user_name}.
alt_responses: You haven't told me your name yet. Try saying 'my name is ...'.
I don't know it yet. Tell me with 'my name is' followed by your name.

intents.name: math
intents.description: The user asks for a basic calculation.
regex: ^(?:what is|what's|calculate|compute|solve|evaluate|how much is|what does)?\s*(?P<expr>(?:\d|[\s+\-*/().%^]|plus|minus|times|multiplied by|divided by|over|into|x|to the power of|squared|mod)+?)\s*(?:=|equal|equals|equal to|\?)?$
responses: {expr} = {result}
That comes to {result}.
alt_responses: I can't compute that one. I handle + - * / % and ^ with plain numbers.
That expression doesn't work. Try something like 12 * 7 or (8 + 2) / 5.

intents.name: joke
intents.description: The user asks for a joke.
responses: Why do programmers prefer dark mode? Because light attracts bugs.
I told my computer I needed a break. It said: no problem, I'll go to sleep.
There are 10 kinds of people in the world: those who understand binary and those who don't.
Why did the developer go broke? Because they used up all their cache.
A SQL query walks into a bar, walks up to two tables and asks: can I join you?
Why was the JavaScript developer sad? Because they didn't know how to null their feelings.
How many programmers does it take to change a light bulb? None, that's a hardware problem.

intents.name: coin_flip
intents.description: The user asks the bot to flip a coin.
responses: I flipped a coin and got {coin}.
{coin}!
The coin landed on {coin}.

intents.name: dice_roll
intents.description: The user asks the bot to roll a die.
responses: You rolled a {dice}.
The die shows {dice}.
It's a {dice}!

intents.name: weather
intents.description: The user asks about the weather, which the bot cannot answer.
responses: I don't have access to live weather data. As a rule-based bot, I can only answer what's written in my rule set.
Weather needs a live data source, and I don't make network calls. A weather API would be the first thing to add if this bot grew up.

intents.name: age
intents.description: The user asks how old the bot is.
responses: I was written in June 2026, so I'm quite new.
Age is a strange idea for a script, but my first commit was in June 2026.

intents.name: location
intents.description: The user asks where the bot is.
responses: I was written in Karachi, Pakistan, and I run wherever this Python script is started.
I live in a Python process. My author is in Karachi, Pakistan.

intents.name: compliment
intents.description: The user says something kind about the bot.
responses: Thank you! That means a lot, even to a set of rules.
That's kind of you to say.
Thanks! I'll pass the credit to my author.

intents.name: insult
intents.description: The user is rude to the bot.
responses: Fair enough. I'm limited to my rules, but I'm doing my best.
Sorry I let you down. Type 'help' to see what I can actually do.
Noted. I'll keep trying.

intents.name: feelings
intents.description: The user asks whether the bot is alive or has feelings.
responses: No feelings here. I'm a Python script that matches your words against a list of rules.
I'm not alive, and I don't think. Every reply I give was written by a person ahead of time.
I'm a program. I don't feel, sleep, or dream, but I do respond quickly.

intents.name: favorite
intents.description: The user asks about the bot's preferences.
responses: If I had to pick, I'd say green. It's the colour of my interface.
I'm partial to Python, since it's what I'm written in.
I don't have preferences, but my author likes clean code and dark mode.

intents.name: acknowledge
intents.description: The user gives a short yes, no, or ok.
responses: Got it.
Alright.
Okay. What next?
Understood.

intents.name: bored
intents.description: The user says they are bored.
responses: I can tell you a joke, flip a coin, or roll a die. Pick one.
Try asking for a joke, or give me a sum like 25 * 4 to solve.

intents.name: apology
intents.description: The user apologises.
responses: No need to apologise.
It's fine, really.
All good. What can I do for you?

intents.name: love
intents.description: The user expresses affection.
responses: That's sweet, but I'm a script. Friends is the best I can offer.
I appreciate it. My heart is a dictionary, and it has room for you as a key.
Friends it is. I'm here whenever you want to chat.

intents.name: repeat
intents.description: The user asks the bot to repeat its last reply.
responses: I said: {last_reply}
Sure. {last_reply}
alt_responses: I haven't said anything yet. Ask me something first.

intents.name: whats_new
intents.description: The user asks what is happening.
patterns: what have you been up to
responses: Nothing new on my end. Same rules, same replies, ready when you are.
Not much. I've been waiting here for a message.

intents.name: user_thanks_bye
intents.description: The user signals they are done but has not used an exit word.
responses: Alright. Type 'bye' when you want to end the session, or just close the tab.
No problem. I'll be here if you come back.
Sure thing. Take care, {user_name}.
